body.target_estimand: \(\tau_P(0)\), defined exclusively as the value at zero of the unique continuous extension of \(\mu_{1,P}-\mu_{0,P}\)
body.estimand_functional: The causal target is \(\tau_P(0)\); it is not defined by an estimator.  For general \(\kappa\ge0\), the established data-only map \(\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)\) from \(\mathrm{thm:first\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\), with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), gives \[c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le Cn^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}.\]  On the bounded-overlap slice \(\kappa=0\), the total data-only map \(\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)\) constructed in \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\) satisfies, for \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(\ell=hk^{-1/d}\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}\mathbb E_P\lvert\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)-\tau_P(0)\rvert\le C\left\{h^\gamma+\ell^S+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha+\sqrt{\frac1{nh^d}\left(1+\frac{k}{nh^d}\right)}\right\}.\]  With \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\) and \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2S)\), its optimized consequence is \[c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\le R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\le C\max\left\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\right\}.\]  Hence the unknown- and supplied-propensity risks have the same rate whenever \(S\ge S_\star\), including equality without a logarithm.  For \(S<S_\star\), the matching exact-uniform lower bound remains open; for \(\kappa>0\), the sharper higher-order frontier beyond the first-order bracket remains open.

sampling_model.design: Known exactly uniform random design on \([0,1]^d\) with \(n\) independent observations.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is strictly positive almost everywhere and equals zero only at \(x=0\) when \(\kappa>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and the uniform design law, but not \(g_P\), \(e_P\), \(\mu_{0,P}\), or \(\tau_P\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Definition 2 and equation (14) give a localized higher-order polynomial R-learner and the bounded-overlap upper balance; Theorems 1--2 pair it with a lower construction over a density-qualified design class whose displayed witness has perforated support.
Theorem 3 bounds a local-polynomial R-learner under bounded estimated propensities and nondegenerate local Gram matrices.
Theorem 2.1 controls the affinity between two convex mixtures when perturbations localize to a measurable partition.
The random-design variance-functional results use local polynomial U-statistics and a fuzzy lower construction to expose a regression-functional elbow.
Theorem 1 analyzes empirical-Gram higher-order influence-function corrections that remove a covariate-density smoothness requirement for average doubly robust functionals.
Theorem 2 gives near-minimax integrated \(L_1\) rates for random treated and control designs under bounded density ratios and contrast smoothness at most one.
Theorem 1 gives the scalar pointwise regression rate under a regularly varying design density through a local-mass balance.
The weak-overlap results derive thresholded average-effect limit laws and a scalar regression smoothness degradation under propensity-tail restrictions.
Corollary 4 gives pointwise RKHS CATE rates without consistent propensity estimation while retaining a uniform positive overlap parameter.

body.tldr: For the full exact local-zero model, the proved supplied-propensity lower bound and total first-order estimator give \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), where \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  On the exact-uniform bounded-overlap slice \(\kappa=0\), a total second-order projection R-learner improves the upper bound to \(C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/[1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta))]}\}\).  It proves the oracle rate once \(\alpha+\beta\ge d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), with no logarithm at equality.  The nuisance-dominated exact-uniform converse below that elbow and the sharper \(\kappa>0\) frontier remain open.

project_justification.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE proves the bounded-overlap contrast frontier over a density-qualified design class, but its displayed least-favorable density removes nuisance-bump transition regions.  Its lower witness therefore does not establish the nuisance-dominated converse on the singleton uniform design, and no current result supplies the full corner-zero frontier for \(\kappa>0\).
project_justification.niche: Exact knowledge of the uniform covariate law makes the localized projection Gram deterministic.  This permits a one-sided second-order R-learner on the full uniform cube, isolating the upper-side nuisance elbow without a covariate-density estimation remainder, while the local-zero geometry remains available for the unresolved weak-overlap problem.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives a total finite-operation second-order estimator on \(\kappa=0\) with risk \(h^\gamma+\ell^{\alpha+\beta}+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha+\sqrt{(nh^d)^{-1}\{1+k/(nh^d)\}}\).  Optimizing it yields the bracket \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\le R_n\le C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/[1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta))]}\}\) and the exact oracle rate above the elbow.  The paper does not claim the missing lower side below the elbow or a solved higher-order \(\kappa>0\) frontier.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, Definition 2 and equation (14), supplies the bounded-overlap higher-order local-polynomial architecture adapted here.  Theorem 3 derives its one-sided exact-uniform analogue with an exact Lebesgue Gram and bounded deterministic pilots.  Their Theorems 1--2 and Definition 1 give the closest full pointwise contrast frontier, but the displayed perforated-support lower witness does not prove the nuisance-dominated lower bound on the singleton uniform design.  Consequently the present high-smoothness match uses Theorem 1's exact-uniform supplied-propensity lower bound, while the below-elbow converse remains open.  Kennedy2023DRCATE supplies first-order local-polynomial R-learner motivation, and LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF and ShenGaoWittenHan2020 motivate projection corrections.  RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, requires partition-local perturbations and does not directly cover the overlapping smooth frames needed to preserve full support.  GaoHan2020 concerns integrated random-design contrast risk; Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesign concerns scalar pointwise regression under a design zero; Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics concerns weak-overlap average-effect inference and scalar regression; and Kim2026RKHSPointwiseCATE retains a global overlap lower bound.  WagerAthey2018CausalForests and GRFReference motivate the application: the official \(\texttt{grf}\) workflow learns nuisance regressions and uses treatment-balance restrictions, but no claim is made that its causal forest attains the rates proved here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The bounded-overlap higher-order upper inequality is now closed, but its rough-nuisance converse is not.  Disjoint partition-local contrast bumps of width \(\ell\) and nuisance-scale amplitude \(\delta=\ell^{\alpha+\beta}\) violate the \(\gamma\)-H\"older bound below the elbow; overlapping smooth squared frames repair transition regularity but fall outside the partition-local premise of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, and retain shared-sign cross terms in fixed-\(n\) product mixtures.  Filling perforated transition holes directly contributes order \(nh^d\delta^2\), which is too large at the proposed nuisance separation.  For \(\kappa>0\), estimated-score variance, noninteger corner powers, and max-norm tie surfaces still require separate upper and lower repairs.
body.honest_scope: For arbitrary \(\kappa\ge0\), the established statement remains the first-order bracket \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  On \(\kappa=0\), the proved second-order estimator improves the upper exponent to \(1/[1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta))]\) below the elbow and attains \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) when \(\alpha+\beta\ge d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\).  The equality case has no logarithm because four finite balance terms have the same power.  No nuisance-dominated lower bound is claimed below the elbow, so whether unknown \(g_P\) changes the minimax rate there remains open; the full higher-order and critical-log frontier for \(\kappa>0\) also remains open.
body.interpretation: At bounded overlap with a known uniform design, pointwise CATE estimation reaches supplied-propensity precision as soon as the combined propensity and control smoothness satisfies \(\alpha+\beta\ge d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), a strictly weaker sufficient condition than \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\).  Below this elbow, the second-order estimator gives a faster certified upper bound, but the absence of a same-class nuisance lower experiment means that an information-theoretic cost of unknown propensity has not yet been proved.  These are minimax statements about local CATE precision, not attainment guarantees for an existing forest implementation.
